standard_prerequisites.name: Root of unity modulo an ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter (and standard usage), a in A such that a^n = 1 mod bA for some n >= 1
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exponent n whose powers of a are units modulo b^m A, and hence modulo b.

core_obligations: Use the hypothesis a^n = 1 mod bA to write a^n = 1 - (a_1 a^{n-1} b + ... + a_n b^n) for elements a_1, ..., a_n in A, forcing the identity 1 = a^n + a_1 a^{n-1} b + ... + a_n b^n (proof lines 14534-14544): the a_i are produced stepwise from the fact that a^{n-i} is a unit modulo b A.

Set B = A[y]/(y^n + a_1 y^{n-1} + ... + a_n) and check that u = a - b y is a unit (proof lines 14546-14564): for a prime q of B lying over p in A, if b in p then a not in p (because aA + bA = A) so u not in q; if b not in p then y = a/b mod q, and the polynomial identity rewrites to b^{-n}(a^n + a_1 a^{n-1} b + ... + a_n b^n) = b^{-n} = 0, a contradiction
proof_roadmap: Write the unit property at each power: 1 - a^n in bA lets one solve for a_1, then a_2, and so on, ending with (1) in the displayed form.
Take B = A[y]/(y^n + a_1 y^{n-1} + ... + a_n) and a prime q of B over p = A cap q.
If b in p, a is a unit mod p so u = a - b y is a unit in B_q; otherwise y = a/b mod q, and substituting the polynomial identity forces b^{-n} = 0 in B/q, absurd.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs a monogenic extension A subset B for which u = a - b y becomes a unit, given aA + bA = A with a a root of unity modulo bA (statement lines 14522-14528). The non-formal content is the polynomial recovery: writing 1 - a^n in bA, one solves successively for coefficients a_1, ..., a_n so that 1 = a^n + a_1 a^{n-1} b + ... + a_n b^n (proof lines 14534-14544); the cleanest part is then the prime-ideal argument (proof lines 14546-14564), where for a prime q of B one either uses a unit mod p or substitutes y = a/b mod q and gets b^{-n} = 0, a contradiction. H2: one explicit lifting step and one short prime-ideal check.
